65-year-old woman with type 2 diabetes diagnosed 2011.
HbA1c 70 mmol/mol (previous 72). Weight 107 kg.
Medication: Metformin 1 g BD, empagliflozin 10 mg, atorvastatin 20 mg.

Social: Married, works part-time. Independent. Has never smoked. Alcohol: ~4 units/week.
BP 146/77.
Plan: Increase gliclazide. Recheck HbA1c in 3 months.

GP CONSULTATION

Social: Lives with husband in a bungalow, independent with ADLs. Pack-years: 5 (stopped 2016). Alcohol: nil.
Plan: Lifestyle advice: weight loss, raise head of bed, avoid late meals. Review 3 months.

PSYCHIATRY OUTPATIENT ASSESSMENT

Past psychiatric history: One previous depressive episode 2016.
Medication: Citalopram 20 mg for 3 months, minimal response.
Personal/social: Lives with wife. Works as a farmer. Wife smokes in the garden. Alcohol: ~20 units/week, advised to reduce.
Risk: Low-moderate; protective factors - family, employment.
Plan: Switch to mirtazapine 15 mg nocte. Refer psychological therapies. Review 4 weeks. Crisis numbers given.

DISCHARGE SUMMARY - General Medicine
Patient: Mrs X, 65 y. Length of stay: 5 days.
Diagnosis: Community-acquired pneumonia, right lower lobe (CURB-65 = 1).
History: Admitted with 4 days of fever, rigors, productive cough and pleuritic chest pain. CXR: RLL consolidation. CRP 165 on admission.
Course: Treated with IV co-amoxiclav and oral clarithromycin, switched to oral on day 3. Brief AKI (creat peak 156), resolved with IV fluids. Mobilising independently at discharge.
Background: T2DM, CKD stage 3a.
Social: Married, works part-time. Independent. Ex-smoker, quit in 2005. Teetotal.
Discharge meds: Co-amoxiclav 625 mg TDS to complete 7 days total; regular meds unchanged.
Follow-up: GP review 1 week; repeat CXR in 6 weeks.

Kind regards,
